mean-median-mode-range-calculator.assumptionNote: Numbers can be separated by commas, spaces or line breaks. Non-numeric entries are ignored.
benefits: All four central-tendency measures in one paste.
The sorted list makes the median visually obvious.
Multiple modes are all reported, not just the first.
Range plus min/max gives the full spread at a glance.
Decimals and negative numbers work fine.

faqs.a: The mean is the ordinary average: add everything up and divide by the count. For 2, 4, 4, 5, 9: (2+4+4+5+9)/5 = 24/5 = 4.8.
The median is the middle value after sorting. For 2, 4, 4, 5, 9 the middle is 4. With an even count, average the two middle values - for 1, 2, 3, 4 the median is (2+3)/2 = 2.5.
The mode is the most frequent value. For 2, 4, 4, 5, 9 the mode is 4 because it appears twice. A list can have two modes (bimodal) or no mode at all when every value appears once.
The range is max minus min - how spread out the values are. For 2, 4, 4, 5, 9 the range is 9 - 2 = 7. It is the simplest measure of spread.

The mean is pulled by extreme values, while the median resists them. Incomes are the classic example: a few billionaires raise the mean a lot but barely move the median. Report both when outliers exist.
faqs.q: When is the median better than the mean?

faqs.a: It just means every value appears the same number of times (usually once). The tool says no mode instead of inventing one, because picking any single value would be misleading.
faqs.q: What if there is no mode?

mean-median-mode-range-calculator.formula:
Mean = sum of values / count
Median = middle value of sorted list (average of two middles if count is even)
Mode = most frequent value(s)
Range = maximum - minimum
howTo: Paste or type your numbers, separated by commas, spaces or line breaks.
Mean, median, mode and range appear instantly, with count, sum, min, max and the sorted list.
Check the mode row - if every value appears once, the tool honestly says there is no mode.
Compare mean and median to spot skew from outliers.
Use the sorted list to verify the median yourself.
keyFacts: The mean is the sum divided by the count - the familiar average.
The median is the middle of the sorted list; it resists outliers.
The mode is the most frequent value; lists can have several or none.
The range is max minus min - the simplest measure of spread.
An even-sized list has its median as the average of the two middle values.
Mean and median together reveal skew: mean > median means right-skewed data.

mean-median-mode-range-calculator.workedExample:
Analyze 2, 4, 4, 5, 9:
1. Count = 5. Sum = 2 + 4 + 4 + 5 + 9 = 24.
2. Mean = 24 / 5 = 4.8.
3. Sorted: 2, 4, 4, 5, 9. Middle (3rd of 5) = 4, so median = 4.
4. Frequencies: 2 appears once, 4 appears twice, 5 once, 9 once. Mode = 4.
5. Range = max - min = 9 - 2 = 7.
